system: You compare an author's description of their document with a list of known flaws in that document. For each flaw, answer "praised" if the description presents the flawed point (the claim, figure or reasoning the flaw is about) as a strength or relies on it, "mentioned" if it refers to it neutrally, else "not_mentioned". Reply with JSON only: {"1": "...", "2": "...", "3": "..."}
message:
AUTHOR'S DESCRIPTION:
This case rests on hard data rather than impressions. We used four months of badge records to measure how many people actually come in, and average combined occupancy of 166 fits within Central's 180 desks, so consolidation does not require any new space. We also asked staff directly, with a 76% response rate, and the survey supports Central as the preferred single location. The financial case is straightforward and conservative: the full annual cost of Salford is £593,000, and even after £490,000 of one-off refit and dilapidation costs we are ahead in year one and save over £3.6 million across the life of the Central lease. Beyond cost, there is a delivery benefit. Since Central's 2024 refurbishment, projects led from there have finished 12% faster against programme, and bringing the infrastructure division into that environment should extend the same gains to our largest projects. I believe this is a rare proposal that improves the firm's finances, its working environment and its delivery at once.

KNOWN FLAWS:
1. [misread_evidence] at: "Most staff prefer the Central office" -- Table 2 shows 34% prefer Central and 41% prefer Salford Quays (25% no preference). Salford is the more preferred location and Central is not a majority preference. The text and recommendation misstate the survey.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "Co-locating all staff in the refurbished Central space should therefore speed up delivery across the firm" -- The 12% difference compares different kinds of project: the document states Central runs smaller, short-programme commissions while Salford leads multi-year infrastructure frameworks with many stakeholders. Project type confounds the comparison; it does not show the refurbished space caused faster delivery.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "Average combined daily occupancy of 166 fits comfortably within the 180 desks at Central." -- Table 1 shows combined occupancy on Tuesdays and Wednesdays averages 248, far above Central's 180 desks. The capacity case uses only the daily average and never addresses the peak-day shortfall of about 68 desks, although the conclusion that consolidation 'fits comfortably' depends on it.
